title: Transactional checkpointed switchover with fast-path rollback
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: implement an upgrade flow for private (VPC) data-plane runtime rollouts that treats each tenant slice as a transactional checkpoint unit to enable deterministic, low-latency switchover and a fast-path rollback that restores a previously-known-good checkpoint without full node evacuation. This ticket designs and prototypes the orchestration and Terraform/IaC hooks to support: (1) lightweight state checkpoints for KV/prefix caches, (2) shadow-apply of new runtime images with synthetic traffic validation, (3) a deterministic handoff protocol for live sessions that preserves KV consistency, and (4) a single-step fast rollback which restores the checkpoint and flips traffic back with minimal token loss and sub-second routing change where possible. The design must integrate with our existing private control plane, operator terraform modules, and health-checking telemetry so upgrades maintain our SLOs and can be audited.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible Terraform plan/module change that adds preflight checkpoint and postapply validation hooks for private runtime upgrades
Runtime operator can create a named checkpoint snapshot for a tenant slice and list/restore snapshots via operator API
Shadow-apply flow validates perf/latency/accuracy against synthetic prompt set; failures block traffic shift
Handoff protocol migrates active requests/sessions without 5xx spikes and keeps token loss < 0.1% for 99th percentile tenants
Fast-path rollback restores the checkpoint and reverts routing within the SLA window (target: 2 minutes worst-case for a single slice), exercising idempotent restore operations
Full audit trail with terraform plan/apply outputs, operator events, and console telemetry linked to the rollout
End-to-end e2e test that simulates corrupt checkpoint and verifies rollback prevents serving bad outputs and resumes previous capacity
tasks: Design checkpoint data model and retention limits (TTL, size cap)
Implement operator API endpoints: create_snapshot, list_snapshots, restore_snapshot, purge_snapshot
Add terraform module hook points: pre_apply_check, post_apply_validation, rollback_trigger
Implement deterministic handoff protocol in runtime: quiesce-accept, in-flight-drain, checkpoint-bind, route-swap
Build synthetic traffic harness for shadow validation that runs during canary and pre-shift
Wire console telemetry: per-tenant snapshot status, validation score, and rollback reasons
Write integration tests for snapshot restore idempotency and partial-restore scenarios
Run staged dogfood in internal VPC cluster and iterate on failure modes
design_decisions: Checkpoint shall be append-only immutable blobs identified by tenant+slice+seq to simplify restore and avoid partial mutation
Retention policy: keep last 3 checkpoints per slice by default; configurable per-customer via module variable
Use off-node durable object storage (S3-compatible) for snapshots to decouple from runtime lifecycle
Handoff will favor in-place KV reconciliation with deterministic merge; avoid full state copy unless mismatch detected
Fast rollback will prefer a single metadata swap and route delta instead of node-wide restart to minimize blast radius
Terraform hook design will be idempotent: running apply twice does not create duplicate snapshots or double-swap traffic
rollout_plan: Preflight: terraform plan against staging with preflight hooks enabled; operator creates initial checkpoints for target slices
Shadow apply: deploy new runtime to a non-serving slice and run synthetic prompt set against shadow endpoint for 30 minutes
Validation gating: require percentile latency/throughput and output-quality thresholds; if gating fails, abort and mark rollback_reason
Incremental traffic shift: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across 5 minute windows with health probes at each step
Checkpoint bind: at 50% shift perform checkpoint-bind to ensure active session pointers moved atomically
Finalization: after 100% stable for 30 minutes, mark checkpoint as succeeded and garbage collect older snapshots per retention policy
rollback_playbook: Automatic trigger conditions: synthetic validation failure, >0.5% 5xx increase, persistent CPU/GPU overcommit for 10 minutes
Operator manual rollback: call restore_snapshot for the most-recent-good snapshot and run route-swap to direct traffic back
Fast-path: if deterministic bind succeeded previously, attempt single-step metadata flip to revert routing; otherwise fall back to evacuation-based rollback
Post-rollback verification: run synthetic checks on restored slice and confirm token continuity and KV consistency
Postmortem: capture terraform plan/apply outputs, runtime logs, and validation harness results into the rollout audit entry
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and console teams. Agreed on snapshot metadata schema and S3-backed storage proposal.
2026-03-02: Operator API skeleton PR opened (internal repo). Initial endpoints and protobufs reviewed; Diego to iterate on idempotency semantics.
2026-03-05: Terraform module hook prototypes added to private-modules repo; added variables for retention and hook timeout. Need security review for S3 credentials flow.
2026-03-09: First shadow apply completed in staging. Synthetic validation failed due to subtle tokenization drift in model variant; aborted and recorded validation artifacts.
2026-03-11: Implemented deterministic handoff proof-of-concept for single-tenant slice; observed near-zero request duplication; working on multi-tenant quorum gating.
test_scenarios: Restore under load: create continuous request stream and run restore_snapshot; assert 99th percentile latency remains within 1.5x baseline
Partial checkpoint corruption: corrupt manifest for middle checkpoint and ensure restore fails safe and triggers fallback evacuation
Concurrent upgrades: two overlapping upgrades for different slices should not interact; isolation test
Terraform double-apply: run module apply twice and assert no duplicated snapshots or route flips
Rollback after failed canary: run canary until validation fails and assert rollback completes within target SLA
qa_checks: Synthetic validation coverage: latency, throughput, response-structure consistency, hallucination regression score
Audit trail completeness: terraform outputs, operator events, console links
Security: ensure snapshot ACLs and KMS-encrypted objects are used; secrets not leaked in logs
Operator authorization: RBAC check to ensure only release engineers can trigger manual restore
Chaos run: random network partitions in staging to assert rollback path handles partial control-plane loss
notes: We intentionally keep the first iteration tenant-scoped to simplify state model and reduce blast radius.
Storage cost estimate: snapshots avg 40MB per slice; with 3 retained snapshots and 10k slices cost ~12TB/year. Finance okayed prototype budget.
Open risk: KMS-per-tenant increases complexity of restore and may increase restore latency. We will evaluate default shared KMS with customer opt-in.
Next steps: complete idempotent restore tests, security review, and run an internal canary for a non-critical customer by 2026-03-18
